title: God Made All His Creatures Free
description: God Made All His Creatures Free in Tonic Solfa to VIENNA, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 189, “The Liberty of the Sons of God”. The compilers changed some of the words, and this is their version.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to VIENNA; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: God made all his crea-tures free; Life it-self is lib-er-ty; God or-dained no oth-er bands Than u-ni-ted hearts and hands.

lines: God made all his creatures free;
Man o'er brute, and man o'er man.
But a better day shall be,
And the wide world's only bands
All God's children dwell in peace,
Love, and Love alone, is Lord.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to VIENNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
